why: The builder brief contains inputs and expected outputs taken from the verifier's probes, so the criterion fails. Builder step 3 names "clamp(-5, 0, 100) === 0", "clamp(140, 0, 100) === 100", "clamp(42, 0, 100) === 42" and "assert.throws(() => clamp(5, 10, 0), RangeError)". Verifier Check 1's case list uses the same first three: [-5,0,100,0], [140,0,100,100], [42,0,100,42]. Check 2 uses the same throwing call, [5,10,0]. The builder is allowed to write its own tests, but here it is handed the checker's exact cases rather than just the bar. Step 2's line "Every name in math.js's module.exports must end up with its own heading" also closely restates Check 3's heading test. Running npm test is allowed and is not the problem.
